title: Review rules
summary: A `.review-rules` file says how risky each changed file is and what to check in it.
description: Not every file deserves the same attention. A repository's `.review-rules` gives each path a risk (low, medium or high) and instructions for whoever reviews a change to it. The app shows the verdict on every changed file and puts the riskiest files first.

stories.as: a reviewer with twenty changed files
stories.want: to know which ones are risky and what to check in each
stories.soThat: my attention goes where a mistake costs most

requirements.text: A file gets the instructions of every rule that matches it. Its verdict is the highest risk among those rules.
Verdicts use the rules on the branch the pull request merges into, never the pull request's own version, so a change can't lower its own risk.
A change to `.review-rules` itself is always high risk.
Approving asks first when a high-risk file isn't marked viewed.
A line of the rules file that can't be read is left out and reported, without hiding the other rules.
A repository without rules offers a prompt for a coding agent to write them.
